summary: The main risk is that the proposed principal-neutral design still crosses several channel-, agent-, and username-scoped contracts. The implementation should first make principal resolution and durable persistence explicit, then change API/UI delivery and migration behavior around those invariants.

suggestions.title: Make durable persistence a required completion outcome
suggestions.rationale: AbstractOAuth2Manager logs and swallows vault-write failures, while JiraOAuthManager swallows CredentialSink failures; the callback can therefore report success with only a Redis copy. Make durable-owner persistence idempotent and observable, and either fail the callback or mark the connection pending for retry before emitting success.

suggestions.title: Resolve and bind the Navigator principal before OAuth starts
suggestions.rationale: The current OAuth state carries channel and channel-scoped user_id, and the Identity Vault sink explicitly no-ops when Slack or Teams has no nav_user_id. Require every new flow to bind a validated numeric Navigator user_id before authorization, or introduce an explicit authenticated linking step; never trust a caller-supplied principal embedded in state.

suggestions.title: Choose and enforce multi-account semantics
suggestions.rationale: auth.user_identities permits multiple accounts per provider, but users_integrations is keyed only by (user_id, provider), the response model exposes one account, and disconnect deletes every account for that provider. Either explicitly enforce one account or add account_id to persistence, listing, start/revoke routes, cache keys, and notifier events; the accepted principal/provider/account key implies the latter.

suggestions.title: Remove agent enablement as a complete contract migration
suggestions.rationale: The current service, handler, persistence layer, API client, and menu still require agent_id and an /enable call that writes user_agent_toolkits. Adding user-level routes beside these paths leaves two conflicting authorization models; retire or explicitly compatibility-wrap the old routes and update cold-session hydration in the same change.

suggestions.title: Persist the metadata the Connections API promises
suggestions.rationale: The current UsersIntegrationRow stores scopes but no expiry, while IntegrationDescriptor does not expose scopes or expiry; persist_credential also does not store expiry. Add non-secret granted scopes, expires_at, refresh/revocation status, and account metadata to the durable read model before implementing the panel.

suggestions.title: Apply PBAC to connect and revoke, not only listing
suggestions.rationale: IntegrationsService performs fail-closed PBAC checks for list_for_user, but start_connect has no request/PBAC parameter and the handler only checks authentication and origin. Add provider- and scope-aware authorization checks to start, disconnect, and any account-selection operation; test denied connect and revoke independently.

suggestions.title: Route WebSocket events by principal, with cross-process delivery semantics
suggestions.rationale: UserSocketManager stores local sockets by mutable JWT username; Redis currently stores presence only, and send_direct_message cannot reach another worker. Index local sockets by the validated principal id and add a Redis subscriber or equivalent per-principal delivery path, defining reconnect, duplicate, and offline behavior.

suggestions.title: Define connection events separately from the existing usage fanout
suggestions.rationale: fanout.py forwards a fixed tuple of usage lifecycle event classes through a Streams publish-only bus and redacts only a usage-specific field. Add explicit connection event types and a dedicated redaction/schema test so token material cannot enter the event payload; keep notifier delivery independent of bus availability.

suggestions.title: Specify an idempotent retry contract for the UI
suggestions.rationale: The current popup and integration components only confirm the connection and tell the user to retry manually; ConnectIntegrationPill receives no original-request or retry callback, and IntegrationsMenu has no WebSocket subscription. Define a retry token/request identity and a completion-driven invalidation or replay API before promising automatic retry.

suggestions.title: Normalize needs-auth at a shared boundary without deleting native details
suggestions.rationale: ToolManager and AgentTalk catch AuthorizationRequired, while CredentialRequired is the broker's canonical signal and currently bubbles through both paths. Use one conversion model/adapter that preserves auth_kind, device-code fields, scopes, and tool name; retain CredentialRequired for surfaces that need native OAuthCard/device-code behavior instead of collapsing all misses into the current web-only shape.

suggestions.title: Keep provider-specific store capabilities explicit during O365 migration
suggestions.rationale: The generic manager uses vault_utils, while VaultTokenSync serves O365 device-code paths with a different session scheme and explicitly tolerates partial writes and persistence failures. Do not force every O365 credential through Identity Vault in S-3a; model interactive 3LO and device-code storage as explicit provider capabilities until the open backend and encryption decisions are resolved.

suggestions.title: Make migration correctness a cross-channel acceptance gate
suggestions.rationale: Existing tests lock in the Slack/Teams first-link no-op and legacy channel dispatch, but do not demonstrate legacy-key migration, principal mapping, cross-channel reads, rotating-refresh durability, or multi-worker WebSocket delivery. Add a matrix that proves a linked user moves from channel keys to the principal key exactly once, an unlinked user is forced to reconnect, and no orphaned credential is treated as connected.
